requirements.text: RRULEs (FREQ, INTERVAL, COUNT, UNTIL, BYDAY, BYMONTHDAY, BYMONTH) expand to the correct occurrences
Invalid or unsupported rules are rejected, and expansion is bounded
Occurrences keep their wall-clock time in the event's time zone across DST changes
EXDATE/RDATE and single-occurrence overrides are applied
Occurrences can be listed for a date window without expanding the whole series
Editing "this and following" splits the series without changing past occurrences

evidence.name: expand-rules: RFC 5545 DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY and YEARLY examples with INTERVAL, COUNT and UNTIL
expand-rules: BYSETPOS and WKST follow the RFC 5545 examples
reject-invalid: malformed and unsupported rules are refused with a specific code
timezone-wall-clock: a weekly 09:00 New York meeting stays at 09:00 local across both DST changes
timezone-wall-clock: a time skipped by spring-forward shifts by the gap; a repeated time uses its first instance
exceptions: EXDATE removes and RDATE adds occurrences, and both survive storage
exceptions: a single occurrence can be moved, retitled, cancelled and restored by RECURRENCE-ID
window-query: listOccurrences returns overlapping occurrences across a calendar
window-query: a window decades into an infinite series skips straight to it
series-edits: 'this and following' splits the series and leaves past occurrences unchanged
sql: 'this and following' split is atomic and keeps the past; 'all' edits and deletes cascade overrides

implementations.notes: No sub-daily frequencies or all-day events (refused, not ignored); no .ics import. PGlite tests run on one connection.

evidence.name: rrule: expansion vectors, invalid rules and limits
rrule: expansion vectors, invalid rules and limits

implementations.notes: UTC only, bounded by a count limit
